title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TESS SUITS UP
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Tess Mahoney, forty-seven, who runs a little laundromat in Marshall, Missouri.
But one sign on the fire station door turned her life inside out.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE SIGN
segments.quote: You are never too old to set another goal or to dream a new dream.
segments.author: Les Brown
lines: The sign said, Volunteer firefighters needed. Tess thought, at forty-seven? That ship has sailed.
Folding towels that night, she heard the speaker Les Brown on the radio:
You are never too old to set another goal or to dream a new dream.
The next morning, she filled out the form. In pen.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: TOO SMALL
segments.quote: What counts is not necessarily the size of the dog in the fight; it's the size of the fight in the dog.
segments.author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
lines: At the first drill, the guys looked her over. She's five foot one.
One said, Ma'am, that hose weighs more than you.
Chief Hal Brody quoted President Eisenhower:
What counts is not necessarily the size of the dog in the fight; it's the size of the fight in the dog.
Tess dragged that hose the whole way. Slowly. But the whole way.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE HEAT
segments.quote: Character cannot be developed in ease and quiet.
segments.author: Helen Keller
lines: Training was brutal. Fifty pounds of gear in a Missouri July.
Taped inside her helmet was a line from Helen Keller:
Character cannot be developed in ease and quiet.
So she climbed the ladder again. And again.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE AIR TANK
segments.quote: Courage doesn't always roar. Sometimes courage is the quiet voice at the end of the day saying, I will try again tomorrow.
segments.author: Mary Anne Radmacher
lines: Then came the air tank test. Tess panicked in the mask, and failed.
That night, her sister texted her a line from the writer Mary Anne Radmacher:
Courage doesn't always roar. Sometimes courage is the quiet voice at the end of the day saying, I will try again tomorrow.
So she did. Slow breaths. Count to four. A week later, she passed.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE PAGER
segments.quote: The secret of success is constancy to purpose.
segments.author: Benjamin Disraeli
lines: Every Tuesday drill, Tess showed up first and left last.
Chief Hal had a card on his desk from Benjamin Disraeli, a British prime minister:
The secret of success is constancy to purpose.
At two one morning, her pager went off. A kitchen fire at the diner.
Tess held the hose steady. Everybody got out. Even the pies.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: NOT A HERO
segments.quote: True heroism is remarkably sober, very undramatic. It is not the urge to surpass all others at whatever cost, but the urge to serve others at whatever cost.
segments.author: Arthur Ashe
lines: Next day, customers called her a hero. Tess turned red as a fire truck.
She remembered the tennis great Arthur Ashe:
True heroism is remarkably sober, very undramatic. It is not the urge to surpass all others at whatever cost, but the urge to serve others at whatever cost.
So she pinned a sign above the dryers. Volunteers needed. Ask me. Two people did.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Dream again. Bring the fight. Get uncomfortable. Try tomorrow. Keep showing up. Serve.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Dream again at any age. Bring the fight. Get uncomfortable. Try again tomorrow. Keep showing up. Serve.
I tried on a fire helmet once. The helmet fit fine. It was the coat that wouldn't close.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
